_why: Iron Rule 2. ONE definition, read by tools/scrub-source-names.mjs (published notes) and tools/yt/brand.py (YouTube descriptions). A second copy is how one of them goes stale - already the failure mode behind two sitemap-condition drifts and a duplicated FAKE_URGENCY in this codebase.
_scope: The rule targets ATTRIBUTION - presenting someone else's book as the source of this site's teaching. Capt. Pahil ruled 2026-08-02 that the bare word is not banned ('oxford is a name, city, street, university'). So these patterns are deliberately multi-word and specific: 'Oxford Aviation', never 'Oxford'.
_plain: Names must be letters, digits, spaces or hyphens only - they are joined into a regex unescaped.
_matching: scrub-source-names.mjs matches case-insensitively and treats a space as any run of spaces, dots or hyphens, and a short all-caps token as initials with optional dots - so 'RK Bali' also catches 'RK-Bali' and 'R.K. Bali'. Added 2026-09-19 after both spellings shipped live past the exact-match check.
